min_enclosing_sphere — 3D bounds op

• Data kinds: points → primitive

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.min_enclosing_sphere(points, refine_iters: 'int' = 1000) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import hull3d; hull3d.min_enclosing_sphere(points, refine_iters: 'int' = 1000) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, ops3d.get("min_enclosing_sphere"))

Usage

Point set (N,3) → the (approximate) minimum enclosing sphere containing every point, {center(3), radius}.

Unlike fit_sphere_3d (sphere fitting) or ransac_sphere / hough_sphere_3d (sphere detection), this solves for the smallest sphere containing all points (minimum enclosing ball, MEB). A 2-stage scheme tightens the radius while strictly keeping "all points enclosed":

1. Ritter (1990) initialization -- roughly take the farthest point pair as the initial sphere, then scan the points; whenever a point lies outside the sphere, grow 1 time to the smallest sphere "containing both that point and the existing sphere" (growth new_r=(r+d)/2 / move the center toward the point by (d-r)/(2d)). Since the new sphere fully contains the old one, 1 pass guarantees that all points are enclosed.

2. Refinement by Bădoiu–Clarkson (2003) core-set iteration -- at iteration i, move the center toward the farthest point q by 1/(i+2). It converges monotonically to the true minimum enclosing sphere (tightening the drift of Ritter, whose radius is too large). Finally the radius is fixed as "the maximum distance from the center", so even after refinement it always encloses all points (being an approximation never makes the radius too small and lets points leak out; it errs on the safe side).

The refined center is adopted only when it shrinks the circumscribed radius below Ritter's (so it is always <= Ritter). It is not the true minimum sphere (the exact solution is Welzl's randomized linear-time method) but a fast (1+ε) approximation.

Parameters

points : array_like (N,3)

Input point cloud (>= 1 point).

refine_iters : int

Number of Bădoiu–Clarkson refinement iterations (default 1000). 0 means Ritter only.

Returns

dict

• center: (3,) float64 -- sphere center (world coordinates).

• radius: float -- radius (encloses all points).

Raises

ValueError

When the shape is invalid, values are non-finite, the point count is 0, or refine_iters is negative (fail-closed).
